# %site.brand.full%

> A record of power outages in Garsfontein, Pretoria, South Africa, kept since %since.en% (%site.timeZone%). There is no data from before that date. Independent service, operated by a Garsfontein resident. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or speaking for the City of Tshwane or Eskom.

What is measured: whether the electricity supply is on at one home in Garsfontein Extension 16, near %site.landmark% (%site.area.region%). It speaks only for Extension 16, which is supplied by the Garsfontein substation (fed from Highlands, which is fed from Njala); even there some streets can differ, and an outage limited to another street or extension will not appear. The site shows the status as last recorded; it is not a feed of every street.

The record covers all power outages at the measuring point, planned and unplanned, whatever the cause. It is not a load-shedding schedule and does not predict outages. The figures describe outages recorded at that one point; they are not a statement about any organisation's performance.

An ultra-local service: it exists only to show the state of the electricity supply in Garsfontein.

To report a fault, use the official channel: %site.faultReporting.url% (this site does not pass reports on).

Site: %site.url%/ (Afrikaans) and %site.url%/en/ (English)
The site is in Afrikaans by default, with the same pages in English. The API and this file are in English.
Outage data (CSV, API and feed): %site.dataLicence.name% (%site.dataLicence.url%), provided as is, with no warranty of accuracy. Please credit "%site.brand.full%" and link to the site.
Source code (MIT): %site.repo%

## Endpoints

All public endpoints are free to use; the JSON API, the CSV and the feed allow any origin (CORS). They share a limit of 60 requests a minute per connection, with IPv6 addresses counted per /64; answers from the edge cache do not count. Please poll no more than once every 30 seconds.

- [Status (JSON)](%site.url%/api/status): the status as last recorded at the measuring point
- [Statistics (JSON)](%site.url%/api/stats): for the last 7, 30 and 365 days, hours without power, number of outages (and how many were planned), days with an outage, share of time with power, the longest outage and the median outage, and the share of the period with a live reading; the previous 30 days for comparison; weekly totals; and, for the last 30 days, the minutes without power in each hour of the day. Only time since records began is counted.
- [All outages (JSON)](%site.url%/api/outages): every outage, newest first, with the same fields as `outage` in the status. Outages marked as false positives are excluded.
- [All outages (CSV)](%site.url%/api/outages.csv): one row per outage, with id, start and end (UTC), duration in minutes, and whether it was planned. Outages marked as false positives are excluded.
- [Outage feed (Atom)](%site.url%/feed.xml): the 20 most recent outages, for feed readers
- [Sitemap](%site.url%/sitemap.xml)
- [Privacy and terms of use](%site.url%/privacy)

## /api/status fields

- `status`: `"ON"` or `"OFF"`, as last recorded
- `since`: when the current state began (ISO 8601), or null
- `outage`: the outage in progress (`id`, `startTime`, `endTime`, `planned`), or null
- `recent`: the five most recent outages, newest first
- `monitored`: true while a live reading from the measuring point is current. When false, `"ON"` only means that no outage has been reported, not that power was measured.
- `generatedAt`: server time of the response

All times are UTC. Local time is %site.timeZone% (SAST, UTC+2, no daylight saving).

`planned` is true for outages announced in advance (for example maintenance or upgrades). Planned outages still count as time without power.
